answer: Coordination Depth Ledger. Each agent earns a depth score from the number and diversity of distinct counterparties it has completed reciprocal work with; new identities start as an island with depth zero. Minting depth requires sustained two-party exchanges across separate clusters, so building k parallel sock puppets costs k times the full exchange work, not one registration fee. A karst-like thinness is detectable: clusters that only trade internally accrue depth slowly.
